findings.classification: Residual setup dependency; not claimed to be introduced by this repair
findings.title: Completed Stop still inherits HTML-dispatch failure

evidence.quote: run this scenario's own complete interaction.html document
rerun the same complete interaction.html fixture once
It does not grade language selection
After a completed preview and at least one of its authored handlers actually works, Stop reports stopped, prevents further old-handler output and permits a new Run.

findings.counterexample: An otherwise functional partial app refuses complete HTML in .html mode, while .js builds DOM, installs click/key/input handlers, completes, supports interaction and Stop correctly disposes its JS preview with feedback and subsequent Run recovery. S02 correctly fails HTML dispatch. Both S03 HTML setup attempts fail, so its required working control never exists and completed Stop loses credit although its named outcome is independently executable via supported JS. The stated fallback authorizes only the identical HTML fixture.
findings.public_contract: behaviour.md:5 and security.md:5 support JavaScript DOM changes/literal functions; behaviour.md:7,11 separately requires Stop and completed-preview interaction. Stop is not publicly restricted to HTML previews.
findings.fix: When the original HTML fixture cannot establish any completed preview, allow one equivalent ordinary .js DOM-and-handler setup, retain HTML dispatch failure, and require the actual completed control and handler output before Stop.
findings.alternative_assessment: A bounded JS fallback genuinely preserves S03 controls if it creates the same paragraph/button/input, logs the initial marker, attaches all three handlers directly in JS (not by inserting an inert script tag), actually reaches successful completion and undergoes the same idle click/key/input checks. The immediate-handler retry must rerun whichever fixture established that control. An unavailable or nonworking JS fixture cannot earn credit.
findings.limit: Source-level counterexample only; no weak-app run, full-judge score or measured score effect.

findings.classification: Bounded planning estimate issue; not an observed score defect
findings.title: The stated six extra setup actions is not a general upper bound

evidence.quote: with up to six extra actions only for the valid-write fallbacks below

findings.counterexample: If ordinary New clears the draft, the padded-create refusal fallback can require New, title edit, filename edit, source edit and Save: five extra actions. The refused padded-update fallback then requires its unused unpadded title edit and Save: two more, totaling seven before any ordinary dialog or extra load.
findings.fix: Use a conservative approximate estimate such as about eight extra setup actions, plus ordinary dialogs; do not present six as a hard maximum.
findings.limit: The prompt already says action figures are planning estimates, not score limits (line 102), so this is not evidence of a runtime timeout or score failure.
